items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: And Otto Hardwick played the -- the release, and I went back to the first eight bars. That was the basic tune of 'Sophisticated Lady'. And I got the terrific check of $15.00 for -- for writing 'Sophisticated Lady'

ctx.x: So what was your first date with the band? Where was the first place you played?

When I came from the Coast, we went to Hartford, Connecticut, where we rehearsed. I didn't play with the band up there. I didn't play with the band at first, because I was the 13th man. And there was so much -- what you call it -- superstition, that oh, no, not 13 men. Had to wait for the 14th man.

And the 14th man was Otto Hardwick, and at that time he was working some where in Washington, doing something, and he couldn't come until later. So my first actual date of playing was at the theater, I think it was the Colonial Theater in Hartford, Connecticut. And of all numbers, I was playing this solo tune, 'Trees'. Scared to death, again.
